Round 3: unverified half ('cache comes before forward') removed from claim and from s4. Manual, Configuration: "The ordering of the Plugins in the Corefile does not determine the order of the plugin chain. The order in which the plugins are executed is determined by the ordering in plugin.cfg." Plugins: "That (static) ordering is defined in plugin.cfg."

"you can modify the ConfigMap for the CoreDNS Corefile to change how DNS service discovery behaves"; default shown as ConfigMap 'name: coredns', 'namespace: kube-system', data key 'Corefile: |'. Capture reads it with jsonpath '{.data.Corefile}'.

Manual: "That file consists of one or more Server Blocks." "Each Server Block starts with the zones the Server should be authoritative for." Root '.': "a server that is responsible for all zones below the root zone". "you can add a plugin by just using its name in a Server Block"; "Other plugins with more configuration options have a Plugin Block, which, just as a Server Block, is enclosed in an opening and closing brace". Lesson makes no claim about chain order (manual: Corefile order does not set it).

Plugin page: "This plugin implements the Kubernetes DNS-Based Service Discovery Specification"; "The kubernetes plugin watches Endpoints via the discovery.EndpointSlices API." Page does not name Services explicitly; execution settles it: echo-new (selector app=echo-new, no Pods) still resolves, so the answer comes from the Service object. k8s docs: a normal Service name "resolves to the cluster IP of the Service."

Capture: 'getent hosts echo-new.network-lessons.svc.cluster.local' answers right after 'service/echo-new created'. Plugin page: "CoreDNS will answer SERVFAIL to any request made for a Kubernetes record that has not yet been synchronized" (answers come from synced API state); cache page: "disable the success or denial cache for the listed ZONES" and the Corefile disables both for cluster.local. Deletion half not executed; the text carries the condition 'once CoreDNS sees it deleted'.

k8s docs: "forward: Any queries that are not within the Kubernetes cluster domain are forwarded to predefined resolvers (/etc/resolv.conf)." Loop plugin: "CoreDNS uses this /etc/resolv.conf as a list of upstreams to forward requests to."
